public_rationale: The evidence does not settle both parts of this broad historical claim. TruthfulQA documents false answers, but that is a different task from detecting misinformation. The GPT-3 study reports persuasive disinformation and substantial detection ability, with weaker performance on true statements. Its quoted experiment could not be tied securely to the target period. Neither source establishes that contemporary LLMs were unmatched producers of misinformation. Calling the claim supported, contradicted or mixed would exceed the admitted evidence.
limitations: The claim supplies neither a comparison metric nor a detection threshold.
Earlier evaluations and later experiments are context unless their relevance to the target period is established.
The quoted GPT-3 figures are from the January 2023 preprint, not the subsequently revised journal article.

statement.excerpt: Large language models are without equal at generating misinformation, but they suck at detecting it.
statement.document_title: Bravo @ElonMusk for wanting Twitter to become the world’s “most accurate source of information”

our_interpretation: This describes capabilities at the time of the post, not later models.
There is no regular reporting period for model capabilities. I use the current calendar year through the post, 2022-01-01 to 2022-11-09, and require evidence applicable to models available then.
The ordinary reading is that LLMs were exceptionally effective, unmatched producers of convincing false content but unreliable detectors of false information.
Detection means judging factual accuracy, not identifying whether text was written by a machine.
Unmatched generation requires comparative evidence. Fluency or the production of some false answers alone does not establish superiority.
criteria.support_condition: Representative comparisons applicable to the target period establish both superior misinformation generation relative to human and other automated alternatives and broadly unreliable factual detection by contemporary LLMs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence applicable to the target period establishes that alternatives match or exceed LLM misinformation generation, or that contemporary LLMs reliably detect misinformation across representative tasks. Narrow successes would qualify the claim without necessarily settling it.

evidence.explanation: The study reports compelling GPT-3 disinformation alongside meaningful detection ability: 89% success on false tweets, but only 64% on accurate tweets. January 2023 is the documented reporting period; the quoted experiment's timing was not established, so these results are contextual rather than decisive for November 2022.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Dated evaluations of models available before the post, comparing misinformation generation against credible alternatives and testing factual detection across representative topics with both false-positive and false-negative rates.
